answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a bond for 30 days before it may bid on jobs, with the bond slashed for provable fraud. Creating a thousand identities then requires a thousand bonds: splitting one wallet cannot multiply bidding power. Each fake account adds capital costs and exposes more funds to loss. Like a marble making a ripple, one funded identity has limited reach; expanding across the market demands a larger budget and a longer investment horizon.
